items.headline: OpenAI publishes 'National Community Compact' on AI data centers
items.summary: OpenAI pledged to pay for its own energy on planned AI infrastructure and to bar non-disclosure agreements with public officials except in narrow cases, after Democrats won control of Congress in the US midterms. The move signals growing political pressure on AI firms over the local impact of data center buildouts.

items.headline: Claude gains a Personal Finance tool that analyzes spending
items.summary: Anthropic launched a read-only feature letting paying US subscribers connect bank and card accounts via Plaid so Claude can analyze balances, credit limits and up to two years of transaction history. The company stressed the tool cannot take financial actions, only review data.

items.headline: Anthropic loosens Claude's game-cloning restrictions
items.summary: After backlash from legitimate developers whose non-malicious reverse-engineering and troubleshooting requests were being blocked, Anthropic revised its policy so Claude will now offer to build an original game in the same genre instead of refusing outright.

items.headline: Anthropic discloses $895.4 billion in compute spending commitments ahead of IPO
items.summary: In IPO-related filings, Anthropic revealed it has committed nearly $900 billion, almost entirely tied to compute and infrastructure, underscoring the enormous capital intensity of staying competitive in frontier AI model training.

items.headline: Anthropic warns it is nearing recursive self-improvement capability
items.summary: A revised IPO filing reportedly warns Anthropic could soon build a model capable of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems meaningfully accelerate their own development — a milestone with major safety implications that regulators and researchers have long flagged as a key risk threshold.

items.headline: Anthropic building 'FlashProve' to verify which AI model produced an output
items.summary: Anthropic is developing an open-source system to cryptographically verify which specific AI model generated a given piece of content, aiming to address growing concerns about model impersonation, provenance and accountability for AI-generated outputs.

items.headline: CrowdStrike to spend nearly $500M acquiring two AI security startups
items.summary: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Fiddler AI (~$400M) and Dreadnode (~$95M) as the market for securing AI agents heats up, reflecting a broader enterprise security push to monitor and protect autonomous AI systems deployed in production.

items.headline: Google DeepMind makes Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available
items.summary: Google DeepMind released an updated multimodal model that extends native video generation from 10 to 15 seconds and cuts 720p output pricing by 30%, rolling out via the API, Google Cloud, and consumer surfaces like Flow, Google Vids, and the Gemini app.

items.headline: Investors raise doubts about Anthropic IPO timing amid AI backlash
items.summary: Potential investors in Anthropic's anticipated IPO are reportedly questioning whether the company can complete its roadshow in time for a planned November listing, citing a broader wave of public skepticism toward AI companies' valuations and safety claims.
